rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the opinion narrow and administrable: enforce a knowing-and-voluntary, textually broad appeal waiver notwithstanding a routine Rule 32(j) advisement and government silence, while preserving established exceptions. Jackson is the most likely dissenter (possibly joined by Sotomayor) focusing on procedural-fairness/reliance at sentencing, with a modest chance of separate concurrences (Thomas/Gorsuch/Alito) emphasizing no constitutional right to appeal and contract-like mutual-assent limits on plea modification.
